messages.subject: Help with grid.arrange
parts:
Hey all,
I need some help debugging. I'm trying to make a loop that will end up with a couple of plots side by side. Everything is working except grid.arrange.
library(gridExtra)
for(j in 1:2){
  for(i in 1999:2000){
    dummy <- subset(myst_only, year == i)
    p <- ggplot(dummy, aes(x = fish_tl, y = count)) +
      geom_bar(stat= "identity") +
      xlab("size (cm)") +
      ylab("Number of sightings") +
      ggtitle(paste(i))
    
    plot_list <- list()
    plot_list[[j]] <- p
 }
    grid.arrange(plot_list, ncol=2, top="work dammit")
}

When I run it, I get the error message "only 'grobs' allowed in "gList" ". I've tried manually entering in plots and it works when I run it like this

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol=2, top = "work dammit")
 
Which leads me to believe that something must be going on with either the way that the list is being created or the way that grid.arrange works with lists. Any help would be appreciated.

Cheers,
David

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Help with grid.arrange
parts:
Hi David,

Looks like you need to put the call to grid.arrange outside of the first loop, that is, after that final bracket.

Scott

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Help with grid.arrange
parts:
Hey David,

Here is a bit of code I wrote yesterday using grid.arrange with a for loop. Ignore everything in the for loop, main point is that I have grid.arrange outside the for loop, and use do.call()

p <- list()
for (i in 1:length(codNames)) {
  pop <- datalist[[i]]
  pop <- pop[pop$AGE > 5,] # plot abundance at older ages to see contrast better
  pop <- pop[pop$YEAR %in% c('1965','1970','1975','1980','1985','1990','1995','2000','2005'),]
    # plot only a few years so it isn't as messy
  #pop$CANUM <- as.numeric(as.character(pop$CANUM)) # convert abundances to numeric
  #pop$YEAR <- as.numeric(as.character(pop$YEAR))
  #pop$YEAR <- factor(pop$YEAR)

  p[[i]] <- ggplot(data=pop, aes(x=AGE, y=CANUM, color=YEAR)) + 
            geom_line() + 
            theme(legend.position='none') +
            ggtitle(codNames[i]) +
            scale_colour_gradient2()
}
do.call(grid.arrange,p)
